themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,100% increase (z-score: 11.72)—signaling a sudden homelessness or street encampment emergency in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway.
evidence: 4 encampment complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 11.72 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Represents most severe spike in dataset across all complaint categories
reporting_angles: Where are encampments appearing and what triggered the sudden surge?
Ground reporting: interview residents near encampments and outreach workers; identify specific locations and populations

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.6 per week—an 860% increase (z-score: 5.42)—indicating rapid deterioration in street-level safety and possible trafficking activity in the district.
evidence: 6 drug activity complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.42 represents highly significant deviation
Concurrent with encampment surge suggests interconnected public safety crisis
reporting_angles: Is drug activity concentrated in specific neighborhoods or corridors?
Interview NYPD, community members, and harm reduction advocates; map complaint locations against transit nodes and encampment sites

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints surged to 9 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.6 per week—a 454% spike (z-score: 7.43)—suggesting widespread mold, pest contamination, or HVAC failures affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: 9 indoor air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.43 indicates highly anomalous pattern
Aligns with long-running heat/hot water crisis (3,310 complaints in 90 days) and plumbing issues (400 complaints)
reporting_angles: Are affected buildings concentrated in specific neighborhoods, and are landlords addressing root causes?
Obtain 311 addresses and conduct building inspections; interview residents about symptoms (respiratory issues, mold visible, odors); check DOB violation history for chronic offenders

themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 100 LAST WEEK from a 20-per-week baseline—a 400% increase (z-score: 4.98)—indicating rapid pavement failure, pothole spread, or infrastructure collapse affecting major corridors.
evidence: 100 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 20 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.98 represents significant statistical deviation
Reflects chronic infrastructure underfunding identified in repeated CB budget requests for DOT streetscape improvements
reporting_angles: Which streets are most affected, and how long has the city known about these conditions?

Visual survey of major thoroughfares (Van Cortlandt Ave, Pelham Parkway); cross-reference 311 complaints with DOB pothole repair records; identify worst corridors affecting bus routes and pedestrian safety

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints surged to 5 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 1,233% spike (z-score: 6.65)—suggesting either aggressive city enforcement activity or a proliferation of unlicensed street vending.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.65 indicates highly unusual pattern
May reflect either new enforcement campaign or unregistered vendor migration into district
reporting_angles: Is this a coordinated city enforcement push, or are vendors responding to economic pressure in other boroughs?
Interview street vendors, DCWP officials, and community members; determine if complaints reflect enforcement actions or quality-of-life concerns about vendor density
